title: Tune backpressure thresholds for long prefill workloads
author: Sofia Ivanova
release_notes: Scheduler: adjust default backpressure/admission thresholds for long-prefill workloads to reduce p99 TTFT while preserving aggregate throughput; adds guardrails and metrics to attribute queueing vs admission stalls.
body:
Title: Tune backpressure thresholds for long prefill workloads

Context
Long-context summarization / retrieval-augmented prompts (large prefill, modest decode) are a top variance driver in the Q1 2026 perf suite (ENG-4824). In baseline sweeps we repeatedly see p99 TTFT spikes correlated with scheduler backpressure entering “hard stop” mode too aggressively once prefill token-in-flight crosses the global watermark. This PR retunes the default thresholds and adds guardrails to protect overall throughput under mixed traffic.

What changed (high level)
- Retune scheduler backpressure thresholds to reduce p99 TTFT specifically in the long-prefill cohort while keeping tokens/s within expected noise for chat/embeddings.
- Split the single prefill watermark into a two-stage (soft/hard) admission control:
  - Soft stage: slows acceptance by applying a small queue delay and preferentially assembling smaller prefill batches.
  - Hard stage: rejects/defers new long-prefill admissions only when the in-flight prefill budget is truly saturated.
- Add a “decode reservation” floor so we don’t starve decode during a prefill-heavy burst (prevents TPOT regressions for streaming chat).
- Emit new metrics tags for backpressure transitions so dashboards can explain TTFT tails (ties into ENG-4826 instrumentation work).

Detailed changes
- scheduler/backpressure:
  - Increase `prefill_inflight_soft_limit_tokens` (default) to reduce premature throttling.
  - Lower `prefill_inflight_hard_limit_tokens` only slightly; keep hard stop available for overload.
  - Change `backpressure_soft_wait_ms` from a flat wait to a capped jittered delay (reduces synchronization artifacts when many workers cross the watermark at once).
  - Add `decode_reservation_ratio` (default 0.15) to keep decode from being starved by large prefills.
  - Tighten the “long-prefill” classifier threshold to better match representative suite bins (>= 8k prefill tokens).
- scheduler/batch assembly:
  - When in soft backpressure, bias toward forming smaller prefill batches to reduce head-of-line blocking and shorten TTFT tails.
- observability:
  - New counters: `scheduler_backpressure_soft_enter_total`, `scheduler_backpressure_hard_enter_total`.
  - New histogram: `scheduler_backpressure_soft_delay_ms`.
  - Tagging: `workload_class={chat_streaming,long_prefill,embeddings}` and `reason={prefill_inflight,queue_depth,decode_reservation}`.

Before/after (perf suite)
Method
- Benchmark harness: representative workload suite v1 long-prefill test (ENG-4824) + mixed traffic smoke (chat streaming + embeddings) to validate no obvious throughput regressions.
- Environment: A100-80GB (us-east), driver 550.54, CUDA 12.4, runtime build redwood@9c3f6e1 (before) vs redwood@c4b0a2d (after).
- Runs: 5x per scenario, discard first run (warmup), report median of remaining 4 runs. Cold and warm cache reported separately; this PR targets cold-path TTFT.

Results summary
Long-prefill cohort (prefill ~ 12k–16k tokens, decode 256)
- TTFT p50: 1.42s -> 1.36s (-4.2%)
- TTFT p95: 3.98s -> 3.21s (-19.3%)
- TTFT p99: 6.87s -> 4.78s (-30.4%)
- Prefill tokens/s (aggregate): 100% baseline -> 98.9% (within noise; see notes)

Mixed traffic smoke (chat streaming + embeddings)
- Chat streaming TTFT p99: +1.1% (noise; no consistent trend across runs)
- Chat streaming TPOT p95: -0.8% (noise)
- Embeddings req/s: -0.4% (noise)

Notes
- The soft-stage delay introduced small increases in queue time at p50 during saturation, but materially reduced p99 by avoiding hard stop oscillations.
- In traces, the “thundering herd” pattern (many workers hitting the watermark simultaneously) is reduced due to jittered delay + smaller prefill batch bias.
- Throughput delta is not statistically significant in our current noise model; see reviewer thread below for rationale.

Risk & rollout
- This changes scheduler defaults. Guardrails:
  - Hard limit remains in place; we are not increasing max in-flight prefill without bound.
  - `decode_reservation_ratio` prevents decode starvation.
  - All knobs are config-driven and can be reverted via fleet config without a rebuild.
- Proposed rollout:
  - Land behind config defaults for benchmark environments first (perf suite + canary).
  - After 48h canary stability, roll out to 10% hosted clusters in us-east only.

Checklist
- [x] Added/updated unit tests for backpressure state transitions
- [x] Added metrics for backpressure enter/exit + delay distribution
- [x] Ran representative suite long-prefill workload (cold + warm)
- [x] Ran mixed traffic smoke (chat streaming + embeddings)
- [x] Added notes to scheduler defaults doc (follow-up PR to confluence planned)

Screenshots / artifacts
- Baseline run IDs: perf-suite/a100-us-east/long-prefill/2026-01-22T03:14Z (before), 2026-01-23T05:02Z (after)
- Trace links (internal): go/trace/sched-bp-longprefill-21541 (before/after pair)

Related
- ENG-4824 (long-context prefill workload)
- ENG-4826 (scheduler instrumentation)
- Slack thread: eng-runtime/1763608899 (p99 regression triage; decision to adjust backpressure)
commits: sched: add soft/hard prefill backpressure thresholds and decode reservation knob
sched: jittered soft backpressure delay + smaller prefill batch bias under pressure
metrics: emit backpressure transition counters and delay histogram w/ workload_class tags
tests: cover backpressure oscillation scenario and decode starvation guardrail
docs: update default scheduler config comments for Q1 2026 baseline runs
review_conversation: Noah Patel (review): The before/after looks good for long-prefill TTFT. Two questions: (1) Why is soft limit increasing but hard limit only slightly changed? (2) Can we prove we’re not just pushing latency into queue time? Please add a metric that attributes TTFT tail to queue wait vs prefill compute.

Sofia Ivanova (author): (1) Soft limit was the main culprit for oscillation; hard limit is still a safety valve for overload so I kept it conservative. (2) Agree — added `scheduler_backpressure_soft_delay_ms` histogram and tagged `scheduler_queue_wait_ms` in the perf harness export. In the after traces, queue wait increases slightly at p50 under saturation, but p99 TTFT drops because we avoid hard stop + re-admission cycles.
Lena Fischer (review): `decode_reservation_ratio=0.15` seems arbitrary. Did you test 0.10 vs 0.20? Also please document the rationale inline in config defaults.

Sofia Ivanova (author): Ran a quick sweep on A100 for 0.10/0.15/0.20. 0.10 occasionally allowed decode starvation during prefill bursts (TPOT p99 up ~6% in one run). 0.20 started to hurt long-prefill throughput more consistently (~3%). 0.15 was stable across runs. Added an inline comment + links to run IDs in `config_defaults.yaml`.

Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Concerned about default changes landing without a canary plan. Please add a note about fleet-config rollback and ensure metrics are low cardinality. Also, are the new tags safe for prod?

Sofia Ivanova (author): Added rollout notes to the PR body and confirmed tags are bounded (`workload_class` enum + `reason` enum). No request IDs. Cardinality should be stable. Rollback is via scheduler config defaults in fleet config; no binary rollback needed.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Any interaction with KV cache / warm runs? We should ensure warm cache numbers don’t regress unexpectedly.

Sofia Ivanova (author): Warm runs are neutral; p99 TTFT warm changes were within +/-2%. The code paths that change behavior are mainly admission gating for large prefills; warm cache reduces prefill compute so it hits backpressure less frequently.

Noah Patel (review): Requested changes: please add a unit test that reproduces the oscillation by crossing soft limit repeatedly; and ensure backpressure state transitions are logged at debug level for perf runs only.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Added `TestBackpressureSoftLimitOscillationDoesNotTriggerHardStop` and gated debug logs behind `SCHED_DEBUG=1` (already only enabled in benchmark harness).
